claim.why_it_matters: The floating-indicators table is shattered into three tables plus stray paragraphs: each description is cut mid-sentence; the indicator name 'compiler directive indicator' is split across two rows; and '-' appears as a separate row whose name is just 'indicator' and whose meaning is a sentence fragment, instead of '"-' and ''-' sharing one row and one description.

verdict.reasoning: Checked the 300 dpi render of PDF page 54 (printed p.30, 6.2.2). The table has three entries: *> comment indicator (items 1 and 2), >> compiler directive indicator, and "- / '- literal continuation indicator. The markdown keeps every word of all three entries in the same order: the full descriptions, '2) an inline comment ... 6.2.2.1, Syntax Rules', 'additional rules in 7.3, Compiler directives.' and 'subject to additional rules in 6.2.2.1, Syntax Rules.'. The PDF itself prints the multi-line cells the way the markdown rows split them: 'compiler directive' over 'indicator', and '"-' over ''-' with 'literal continuation' over 'indicator'. Nothing is missing, misquoted, reordered or attached to the wrong indicator. The defect is OCR table segmentation, where wrapped cell lines became extra rows and loose paragraphs. That is a formatting and line-wrap artifact that does not change meaning, so the claim is rejected.
